content:
Applications open until 18 October (NEW DATE!)

The Sustainability in the Built Environment Award 2024 aims to promote and recognise good practices, as well as raise awareness among industry and public institutions of the need for knowledge and innovation in the field of sustainability and circularity in the Built Environment.

This initiative, now entering its 2nd Edition, follows on from the work carried out by BUILT CoLAB under the Circularity in Construction project, which made it possible to diagnose the current state of the topic in Portugal and to understand that the AEC sector needs a push to increasingly adopt sustainable measures in the built environment.

Currently, at European level and when considering the whole life cycle, the built environment is responsible for around 50% of all raw materials extracted from nature, more than 30% of the waste generated and more than 35% of greenhouse gas emissions (of which around 12% are attributed to material extraction, manufacture of construction products, and building construction and renovation).

In order to meet the challenges related to climate change and the growing scarcity of natural resources, the European Union, of which Portugal is a member, has been promoting the adoption of guidelines that foster the principles of sustainability and circularity across all economic sectors. To this end, there is increasing support for digitalisation (e.g. the twin transition – the ecological and digital transition), while various paradigms are shifting, such as treating construction and demolition waste as a resource.

The Sustainability in the Built Environment Award therefore wants to once again contribute to the discussion of this topic and continue to encourage innovation by showcasing the best national practices, giving them prominence and recognising the merit of the entities that implement them. With this goal, applications will be assessed on their innovation, relevance and contribution to advancing knowledge in two categories: Sustainability and Circularity.

Applications run until 18 October 2024, and the winners will be revealed in November (date and venue to be announced).

Organisation

The 2nd Edition of the  Sustainability in the Built Environment Award 2024 is an initiative of BUILT CoLAB, the Collaborative Laboratory focused on the Twin Transition of the AEC Sector, with the aim of driving the sector to adopt more sustainable measures in the Built Environment.

Find out here about the winners of the 1st Edition of the Sustainability in the Built Environment Award 2022.

Regulations

Categories you can apply for

The Sustainability in the Built Environment Award 2024 will distinguish two categories:
• Sustainability;
• Circularity.

General conditions

Participation in the Sustainability in the Built Environment Award requires that:

• Eligible candidates, for the various awards, are any persons or entities, public or private, individual or corporate, that are headquartered or established in Portugal and/or generate direct benefits for Portuguese society. International experiences developed by candidates are also considered, provided it is demonstrated that the candidate played (or plays) a leading role;
• Applications must represent initiatives or projects developed by the applicant with verifiable and demonstrable results. To this end, candidates must have authorisation from the authors of the projects to disclose the submitted material;
• The initiatives/projects presented may still be ongoing or must have been completed in the year prior to this edition;
• The initiatives or projects submitted must represent a significant impact on the development of the themes associated with each of the categories described in these Regulations, whether in the transformation of activities, business or society;
• Candidates authorise the free use and disclosure of all submitted information, their name and image;
• Candidates agree to all the clauses of these regulations.

Eligibility Criteria

The following entities are eligible for each category:

Category “Sustainability in the Built Environment”:

• entities that have promoted innovative construction methods or technologies in the development/project submitted for application, taking into account its sustainability (environmental, economic and social factors) – for example, concern for LCA and LCC studies for the whole life cycle and/or;
• entities whose project/development has represented significant savings in terms of embodied energy [MJ/m2] and greenhouse gas production [kg CO2 eq./m2] compared to other similar solutions and/or constructions and/or;
o entities that have promoted the application of naturally based and naturally renewable materials and/or solutions with genuine advantages, across the whole construction life cycle, compared with other solutions, via benchmarking and/or;
• entities whose development/project has promoted greater knowledge of the overall environmental footprint of that construction, as well as of the materials used, including energy efficiency as a relevant element to consider in a whole life cycle analysis.

Category “Circularity in the built environment”:

• entities that have implemented circular economy principles in their projects, with a view to keeping construction products, components and materials at their maximum utility and value over time, contributing to the regeneration of nature, based on factors such as durability, adaptability and waste reduction. An example of this would be considering and designing, from the outset, construction solutions that can be dismantled and reused and/or;
o entities that have promoted the efficient use of renewable natural resources, as well as the reduction of waste production, thereby promoting a paradigm shift in the AEC sector and/or;
• entities that have promoted good demolition/deconstruction practices, e.g. sorting, or the development of technological solutions that contribute to increasing the rates of recovery, reuse and/or recycling of construction and demolition waste and/or;
• entities that have promoted technological advancement or the development of methodologies for either eliminating hazardous substances or upcycling materials, demonstrating the importance of the paradigm shift needed for waste to be seen as a resource and/or;
• entities that have valued an integrated and collaborative vision of the project/development, based on circular economy principles applied to the AEC sector, using innovative technologies and/or methodologies, contributing to the sustainable advancement of the sector and/or;
o entities that have used criteria associated with Green and/or Innovation Public Procurement.

Important Dates

• Application submission period: until 18 October 2024;
• Announcement of finalists: 31 October 2024;
• Submission period for finalists' videos explaining the application and/or providing additional clarifications on the application already submitted: 1 to 29 November 2024;
• Awards Ceremony: January 2025 (date and venue to be confirmed).

Assessment Stages

i. Acceptance of applications: The submission of the Application, together with the corresponding additional documentation, must be made by 15 September 2024 at 11:59 pm;
ii. Selection of finalists: the Jury will assess which applications will proceed to the next stage, based on the form submitted by the candidate and taking into account the respective assessment criteria described in these Regulations;
iii. Final presentation of finalists (optional): finalist candidates must produce a video lasting no more than 5 minutes and/or supporting documentation, in which they must explain details of their application and/or answer specific questions identified by the Jury;
iv. Selection of Winners: based on the initial documentation and the video developed by the candidates, the Jury will select the Winner and the Honourable Mention (which may or may not exist depending on the quality of the proposals) for each category;
v. Announcement of winners: after the Jury has selected the winning candidates within each category, these will be announced at the Awards Ceremony.

In all situations not covered by these Regulations, any decision shall be the responsibility of the Jury.

Conditions for Submitting an Application

• Applications are made on this web page by fully completing the application form provided below, corresponding to the category the applicant wishes to enter. All information provided on the site will be updated by the organisation whenever necessary.
• Complementary documentation (i.e. all documents that candidates consider important to add, to the benefit of their application) must accompany the application form and also be sent in digital format (file or compressed folder in .zip format, not exceeding 5MB).
• Candidates may submit an application to more than one category.
• Projects that have won in previous editions may not apply.
• The application of professionals, companies or institutions that are, in any way, in a conflict of interest with any member of the Jury for the categories in question will be assessed by the other members of the jury, with the member with the conflict of interest excluded from the assessment. 
• Once the application form has been completed, the complementary documentation uploaded and the application submitted, an automatic e-mail will be sent to the application e-mail address confirming this submission.

Assessment Process and Criteria

– The process of accepting, verifying the eligibility of and assessing applications submitted to the PSAC will be verified by BUILT CoLAB, to ensure compliance with the criteria established by these Regulations, guaranteeing the transparency of the entire process.

– The Jury, for each category, will be responsible for assessing applications according to previously established criteria, as follows:

  1. Technical quality of the application (in terms of objectives, impact, benefits and associated costs) – 30%;
  2. Innovative nature and ability to combine different technologies and applications of the initiative/project submitted for application and its relevance to the current context of the category applied for – 20%;
  3. Significance, benefits and durability of the (verifiable) expected or achieved impacts within the category applied for – 20%;
  4. Scalability and potential applicability of the initiative/project per se and to other areas and/or initiatives/projects or even other sectors – 20%;
  5. Contribution of digitalisation to structuring and making available the information associated with the initiative/project submitted for application, thereby enabling the dissemination of good practices in the AEC sector – 10%.

* In the event of the same project applying to both categories, the jury may give a conditional assessment in order to allow for greater plurality of projects to be publicised.

Jury

The Jury for the Sustainability in the Built Environment Award 2024 will be made up of the following members:

• BUILT CoLAB: Rita Moura (Chair of the Jury);
• AEC Cluster/Portuguese Construction Technology Platform (PTPC): Jorge Nandin de Carvalho;
• Laboratório Nacional de Engenharia Civil: Laura Caldeira;
• Ordem dos Arquitetos: Marlene Roque;
• Ordem dos Engenheiros: Fernando de Almeida Santos;
• APA: Ana Cristina Carrola;
• AICCOPN: Manuel Reis Campos;
• IMPIC: Fernando Batista.

Award

The finalists of the Sustainability in the Built Environment Award will be announced on the BUILT CoLAB website and will be entitled to:
• A Trophy for Winners;
• An Award Certificate;
• A digital Award seal for publication on digital channels;
• Wide-ranging publicity.

The Awards will be presented, conditions permitting, at an Awards Ceremony organised by BUILT CoLAB, on a date, at a venue and in a format to be announced.

Contacts

If you have any further questions, please contact the organisation by e-mail at info@builtcolab.pt.
